mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing the cost of capital and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings declines and negative equity returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate rises by more than 0.5pp in 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month indicate a contraction in consumer and residential demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the same month but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% in one month signals an imminent slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% in a month but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A nonfarm payroll employment level above 100,000 thousand persons indicates a robust labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS remains above 100,000 thousand for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year increase in CPI exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive monetary stance, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY increase exceeds 3.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate a broad-based economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Both HOUST and GDPC1 decline in the same period but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), an increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% per annum signals a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS rises above 4.0% but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such events.
